title: Territory-aware routing: customer gating and fallback model plan
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Implement territory-aware routing controls that allow ops/PMs to declare per-customer routing gates and fallback model variants to ensure data locality and regulatory compliance. This ticket scopes the engineering deliverables for: (1) a configurable customer gating rule that can enforce territory constraints (e.g., route to EU-only infra), (2) an ordered fallback chain of compatible model variants when the primary tier is unavailable, and (3) auditing hooks for data residency decisions. We must support allowlists and denylists per customer and per routing tier, plus a policy precedence model that is expressive but auditable.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Admins can create a 'territory gate' for a customer that enforces routing to a regional deployment (example: EU region only) via Console and API.
2. Routing engine evaluates gates and chooses primary route or falls back to the highest-priority compatible variant; fallbacks include same-region compatible quantized variants when available.
3. Requests that violate a deny rule are rejected with a clear 403 + explainable policy code and audit entry.
4. Every routing decision logs: customer_id, matched_rule_id, chosen_route, fallback_chain, decision_timestamp, and matched_policy_version.
5. Integration tests cover: allowlist happy path, deny path, tier-saturated fallback, and multi-region failover.
6. E2E performance regression <=5% p95 latency increase for routed requests vs baseline.
7. Markdown runbook added to the repo describing how to add/edit customer gates and rollback steps.
tasks: Design policy schema and precedence rules (policy-engine team)
DB schema migration to store per-customer gates and versions
Routing engine evaluation path changes to consult territory gate service
Implement API endpoints for CRUD on customer gates
Console UI: customer detail page toggle + rule editor (frontend PR)
Audit log pipeline: add structured fields for routing decisions
Run security review and compliance sign-off
implementation_notes:
Policy model: simple ordered list of predicates with explicit precedence. Each predicate can be 'region-only', 'tier-allowlist', 'tier-denylist', or 'model-variant-constraint'. Store a policy version for safe rollouts. Evaluate rules in a short-circuit loop to minimize latency.
Fallback semantics: define compatibility matrix between model variants (e.g., gpt-neox-20b-8bit is compatible with gpt-neox-20b-q8 but not with a smaller architecture). Implement a compatibility resolver component to emit an ordered fallback list before attempting route selection.
KV cache: ensure cached responses tagged with 'residency_scope' to prevent cross-region reuse.
Migration plan: add new columns with defaults, backfill rules for high-usage customers, feature-flag rollout for the routing engine, monitor via canary in eu-region first.
rollback_plan: Feature-flag gated on routing-service. To rollback: flip flag to old behavior, trigger a lightweight config sync, and invalidate any in-memory route caches. If DB schema causes issues, run reversible migration scripts provided in the PR. Post-rollback: run audit compare script to ensure decisions match baseline for a sample window.
